company: NextBoat Inc. (formerly Off The Hook YS Inc.)
market_holds: No option chain and no usable consensus: aggregators show zero analysts for Q3 EPS (TipRanks) and one stale $10 target from the IPO-era ThinkEquity note, so there is no number to beat beyond the company's own FY2026 revenue guide of $165-170M, maintained on 2026-08-13 (H1 was $88.9M, so H2 needs $76-81M). The tape has done the pricing: spot $1.37 (sealed 2026-11-16), -26.1% over 20 sessions, -64% from the 52-week high, a print of $1.00 at the 2026-11-12 open, then a +20% bounce on 112k shares on 11-13. Market cap about $34M on 25.14M shares. 20-day realised vol 98% annualised, about 6.2% a day; turnover about 36k shares a day (roughly $50k), so the opening print is thin and noisy. The last amc print (Q2, 2026-08-13, record revenue +88%) opened -4.8% (2.00 vs 2.10, Yahoo bars). The line the stock seems to trade on is liquidity and dilution, not revenue: since the last call the company has taken a $510k 10% OID convertible with a reset (Aug 14), a 15% 90-day subordinated bridge secured by the chairman's pledged shares with mandatory prepayment from the sale of seven named used boats (Oct 9), and a 12.99% $5M revolver against 7.87M more pledged shares (Oct 22), and replaced its CEO (Sep 28). All of that is public and the 20-day slide is the price absorbing it.
view: A micro-cap pre-owned boat dealer roll-up whose Q3 headline revenue will look large against a weak base (Q3 2025 was $24.0M; Q2 2026 was $59.1M with the Apex and Bellhart acquisitions), so the release will very likely lead with triple-digit or near-triple-digit growth, as Q2 did. The Q2 release led the same way and the stock still opened about -5%, because the market was reading losses, interest cost and cash. The Q3 picture on those lines should be worse: cash was $7.7M at June 30 and falling, the Q3 and October financings were expensive, short-dated and secured on the controlling holder's stock, the industry quarter was soft (MarineMax same-store sales -5.7% for Jul-Sep), the new CEO's first public framing was capital allocation and inventory turns ('sharpen focus on the core pre-owned business'), and a company that issued frequent operating-metric releases in the spring has issued none since September. A new CEO reporting his first quarter has an incentive to reset the guide, and the 10-Q may add going-concern language that the Q2 10-Q did not carry (EDGAR full text finds 'substantial doubt' only in an acquired entity's financials). Against that, the stock has already fallen 26% in four weeks and touched $1.00, so much of the deterioration is visibly in the price, and a thin promotional micro-cap can pop on a revenue headline. I lean down modestly but cannot show a mechanism the price has not got to, and the opening print on $50k a day of turnover is close to noise.

recommendation.reason: The plausible negatives (worse losses and interest, a possible guide reset by a new CEO, possible going-concern language) follow from public financings and a 26% four-week slide that already prices distress. With no consensus to beat and no fresh data on Q3 units or revenue, I cannot show what the price does not hold, and the opening print in a stock that trades about $50k a day is too noisy to bet at 58%.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A reiterated $165-170M guide with Q3 revenue above about $45M and a statement that liquidity is adequate without equity, which would make the up case real; conversely a withdrawn guide plus going-concern language would firm the down case.

key_evidence.shows: Q2 revenue $59.1M (+88%), H1 $88.9M, net loss $2.1M, cash $7.7M (from $12.4M), floorplan $51.6M, FY26 revenue guide $165-170M maintained
Q2 amc print opened -4.8% (2.00 vs 2.10); stock -26% in 20 sessions, $1.00 open on 11-12, bounce to $1.40 on 11-13; ~36k shares/day
$2.2M 15% subordinated note, 90-day maturity, secured by chairman's pledged shares, mandatory prepayment from sale of seven named pre-owned boats
$5M revolver at 12.99%, $2M drawn Oct 22, 7.87M chairman shares pledged (31% of outstanding), 25.14M shares outstanding
$510k 10% OID convertible at $1.785 with six-month reset to lower bid price, plus warrants
CEO Brian John stepped down effective Sep 28; Ross Tannenbaum appointed CEO; this is his first quarterly report
New CEO frames priorities as capital allocation, inventory turns of 5-7x as a long-term target, limiting dilution from a common stock offering; no Q3 metrics
MarineMax Jul-Sep 2026 same-store sales -5.7%, decline mainly in boat sales
No operating-metric release since the Q2 print, only governance, financing and date releases, from a company that issued metric releases in the spring
Q3 EPS consensus based on zero analysts; no meaningful bar
'Substantial doubt' appears only in an acquired entity's financials (8-K/A, June 2026), not in NXB's own 10-Qs to date
H2 needed for guide = $165-170M minus $88.9M = $76-81M; Q3 seasonal ratio last year (24.0/31.3) applied to Q2 gives about $45M, so the guide is reachable but not with margin

self_critique: The down case rests on facts that are all public and visibly priced: a four-week slide of 26% and a $1.00 print are exactly what a market pricing distress looks like. The release will lead with a big yoy revenue jump against a $24M base, and a thin, promotional, retail-held micro-cap can gap up on that headline, as it did after the FY2025 release (Apr 1 opened +3% and closed +22%). The 11-13 bounce on three times normal volume may also mean someone is positioned for a better print. I also cannot rule out that the new CEO keeps the guide and that the revolver makes liquidity look adequate.
approach_notes: P4 (priced-in is a claim to prove) helped: the financings were public and the tape plainly moved on them, so I could show they were priced rather than assume an edge. P3's push for fresh data mostly found nothing for a thin micro-cap with no coverage; the absence of company metric releases was the only fresh signal, and P5 rightly kept it a lead.
